location_help_server: Use an isolated browser on the computer running the PandaMate service. If the service runs elsewhere, work happens there.
location_cloud_unconfigured: This workspace has no managed cloud computer yet. You can also connect your own cloud server.
location_help_remote: Connect a computer you have set up, such as your Mac, a Linux computer, or a cloud server.
location_server: Execution on the PandaMate server computer
location_none: Choose a work computer to use computer tools
location_pairing_summary: Pair a computer you manage to use it for Bot work.
location_pairing_policy: Approvals stay with the task requester. Use the Bot’s screen to watch work or take over privately when supported.
location_cloud_recovery: Refresh the status before retrying. If the cloud computer stays unavailable, ask your deployment administrator to check its binding and connection.
pair_setup: Set up a Mac, Linux computer, or your own cloud server
pair_install: On the computer you want to pair, open the PandaMate source folder in an interactive terminal and install its dependencies.
pair_run_command: Run the pairing command from that folder.
pair_desktop_setup: Build the Mac helper with npm run desktop:build first. Grant Screen Recording and Accessibility on that Mac to use desktop control.
pair_use_output: Keep that terminal open. Paste the address and token it prints below. Stopping the command invalidates that token.
pair_network: A loopback address works only when PandaMate’s service runs on the same computer. From another computer, use an HTTPS address that the PandaMate service can reach through your configured network.
pair_origin: If your deployment uses a public HTTPS origin, add --origin with that exact origin to the command.
pair_copy_failed: Select the command and copy it manually.
pair_address_help: Use HTTPS or a loopback HTTP address. Keep the connection token out of chat.
pair_recovery: Check that the work process is running, the service can reach its address, and the token and workspace match. A previously configured computer may require its own setup guide.
pair_per_screen: Ready status checked when preparing the Bot’s screen
local_shared_browser: Bots share one isolated browser on the server computer and take turns using it.
shared_screen_description: Bots take turns using this screen.
remote_shared_browser: Bots take turns using the isolated browser on this computer.
shared_desktop_description: Bots take turns using the desktop on this computer.
ask_owner_to_prepare: Ask the workspace owner to prepare this Bot's screen.
